Subject: Initial proposal on liability cap structure

Markus / Laura —

Thanks for sending the redline earlier. Our legal team reviewed Redwood_MSA_v3.2 and proposed the attached alternative to the liability section. High level: BrightBridge is pushing for an annualized cap (per 12-month billing period) tied to the fees paid in that period rather than a single aggregate cap across the term. They think that approach better matches our usage variability and limits runaway exposure if there is a multi-year deployment ramp.

Key asks from BB:
- Annual cap = 3x fees paid in the 12-month period (subject to carve-outs)
- Aggregate cap across the entire term to be 6x total fees (as a floor for catastrophic events)
- Explicit carve-outs for willful misconduct and data breaches (they want certain exclusions to remain)

Attached: Redwood_MSA_v3.2_redlines.pdf (their redline) and a proposed OrderForm that reflects estimated first-year fees.

Can we review internally and propose a counter? We'd like to close the commercial terms this week if possible.

Thanks,
Jamie

BrightBridge Analytics

Markus —

Thanks for the summary. Quick thoughts from legal and contract ops after a first pass:

1) Annualized vs Aggregate
- Annualized caps (by billing window) are reasonable from a cash-flow and fairness perspective, but they complicate incident attribution across windows (e.g., an incident straddling a billing period).
- We can accept annual caps if we define a clear measurement period (rolling 12 months measured from invoice date) and specify how cross-period incidents are allocated (pro rata or assign to the period when customer suffered majority impact).

2) Multipliers
- 2x annual fees is defensible for operational failures; 3x is at the high end — avoid committing 3x as standard since it increases our tail risk.
- Proposal: offer 2x as standard and permit 3x with a one-time executive approval/discount exception tied to strategic accounts. Document the exception in the Order Form as a negotiated field.

3) Aggregate floor (term cap)
- Accept an aggregate cap at 4x–6x total fees as a compromise; recommend 4x unless BrightBridge insists on 6x — we can trade to pricing/commitment.

4) Carve-outs
- Keep the typical carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For data breaches, avoid a full exclusion; instead, tie remediation obligations and allow certain breach-related damages to be excluded up to a defined cap and subject to insurance offsets. Ask Security for input on required controls and incident response SLA language.

5) Suggested redline language (short form) — add to MSA: 
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer's aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) two times (2x) the fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) month period preceding the claim, or (ii) $250,000; provided that for Strategic Customers, Executive Approval may increase such cap up to three times (3x) the fees paid in the twelve (12) month period. Certain liabilities excluded by Section X (willful misconduct) shall not be subject to the foregoing cap."

Next steps: Karthik, can you model expected exposure for BB under 2x vs 3x annualized caps using the OrderForm projections? Also, Marissa, please coordinate with Security for a short note on breach carve-outs and required controls. I will prepare a concise counter to send to BrightBridge.

Laura Bennett
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Jamie Holt <jamie.holt@brightbridge.io>, BrightBridge Legal <legal@brightbridge.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal on liability cap structure — Redwood counter

Jamie —

Appreciate the quick review and the constructive framing. After internal alignment with legal and contracts ops, Redwood can move toward an annualized cap model with the following counter-proposal designed to balance BrightBridge's cost predictability and Redwood's operational risk: 

Summary counter: 
- Annual cap: default = 2x fees paid in the previous twelve (12) months (rolling, measured from invoice date).
- Strategic exception: with documented executive approval, annual cap may be increased to 3x fees for customers meeting strategic criteria (to be listed in the Order Form).
- Aggregate term cap: 4x total fees paid during the term (this is intended as a safeguard for catastrophic, multi-period events).
- Carve-outs: gross negligence and willful misconduct remain subject to exclusion. For data security incidents, Redwood proposes a hybrid approach: breach-related direct damages are subject to a separate sub-cap equal to 1x annual fees, plus we commit to robust incident response procedures and coordination; we will also credit proceeds from applicable insurance against damages.

Operational notes: 
- We will define "fees paid" as invoiced and collected amounts for licensed services during the measurement period.
- For incidents spanning multiple billing windows, damages will be allocated pro rata across affected windows unless parties agree otherwise in writing.

Attachments: attached is a clean mark showing the proposed liability paragraphs and an Order Form placeholder for the executive-exception field. (See Redwood_MSA_v3.2_redlines.pdf and OrderForm-BrightBridge-0627.xlsx attached)

If this is acceptable in principle to BrightBridge, we can have legal trade space: aggregate cap ↔ pricing/term length/commitment levels. If BrightBridge wants to keep 3x as the default, we'll need to shift some commercial terms (higher one-time setup fee or minimum annual commit).

Proposed next step: Please confirm whether BrightBridge will accept 2x annual + 4x aggregate as our starting point and whether you require inclusion of strategic-exception language in the Order Form now or as a separate addendum. If agreed, Laura will produce a tracked redline of the MSA and Karthik will produce a short exposure memo.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Markus
